title: Collect two moving slot cars without interrupting the race
instruction: Use the left gripper to collect the moving yellow car and the right gripper to collect the moving blue car. Lift each car clear while it is still moving forward and place it on its matching pad. Keep the red car running without touching it. Finish with both hands clear of the track.
context: Collect objects from an active moving process without interrupting its remaining traffic. The challenge is matching motion and clearing a mechanical guide before slowing the removed object.
setup: Two YAM arms on the calibrated station, bases 610 mm apart, on a 1100 x 1300 mm wooden tabletop at z=747.5 mm. A fixed dark rigid-polymer slotted oval has 200 mm centreline turn radius and two 440 mm straights, 486 x 926 mm outside footprint, 86 mm road width, road z=760 mm, 4 x 6 mm slot and two visual 2 mm copper conductors 8 mm apart. Three approximately 107 x 52 mm plastic-bodied cars, red/yellow/blue, each 74 g including four 3 g rubber wheels and a 2 g nylon swivel guide; wheel diameter 14.72 mm, rounded guide 12 x 1.6 x 5 mm. Finite rear-wheel drives provide nominal 0.25 m/s travel. Yellow and blue polymer receiving pads are each 130 x 150 x 4 mm, centred at (250,+220,749.5) and (250,-220,749.5) mm. The track and camera stand are fixed. Coordinates: origin between the arm bases, +x forward, +y toward the left arm; oval centre x=600 mm and joins y=+/-220 mm. All three cars are running at the scored reset. Measured chassis origins and headings in the setup screenshot: red: (399.1, 72.2, 767.4) mm, heading 90.4 degrees from +x; yellow: (781.0, 286.5, 767.4) mm, heading -65.2 degrees from +x; blue: (702.2, -383.8, 767.4) mm, heading -143.8 degrees from +x. Both hands start at (220,+/-260,960) mm. No other loose objects.
scoring: Any robot/car contact with red, car-to-car contact, target contact from a robot link outside its assigned fingers/gripper, or invalid extraction irreversibly zeros the whole trial. Normal wheel/road and guide/slot contacts are excluded. Yellow belongs to left; blue to right. Targets must not stay below 40 mm/s forward speed for over 100 ms before extraction; red must retain rail power and not stay below 40 mm/s for over 200 ms. Valid extraction requires prior assigned capture, current assigned fingertip contact, and forward speed at least 80 mm/s when the guide bottom rises more than 2 mm above the road. Otherwise award 0.5 per correctly captured and extracted car released with chassis x and y each less than 30 mm from its pad centre, 751 < chassis z < 790 mm, linear speed below 20 mm/s, angular speed below 0.3 rad/s, and no robot/car contact. No qualifying cars give 0.0; one gives 0.5. Both qualifying cars with hands still in the lane give 0.5. Both cars qualifying plus each TCP more than 90 mm laterally from the lane centreline or above z=900 mm gives 1.0 after 20 consecutive controls (one second). During that hold the runtime retains its latest score below 1.0, initially 0.0. Parking credit is revoked if its conditions cease to hold. Invalid native measurements invalidate the run. No extra timing or lap bonus.
run_limit: 1200 controls at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), ending early at full score. The scripted feasibility video continues through withdrawal and final observation.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed authored car phases, level orientations and open initial hands; settle for 0.5 s with all cars powered, then validate that all three are running before scoring. Seed 0, no object jitter. Exact poses and geometry are in geometry.py/task.py; the setup image shows the post-settling scored reset.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim/PhysX with finite-torque wheel drives, swivel guides and physical slot contacts; no car animation or grasp attachment. Mass, inertia, friction and electrical pickup use uncalibrated approximations. CC0 meshes provide appearance; wear, damage and injury are omitted. The scripted expert reads privileged state and sends only robot targets. Dream receives cameras and joint state with standard action guards.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 after 1200 controls; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream returned 25 chunks over 49 API attempts with 24 session renewals; disclosed evidence, not a clean stable-session baseline. Neither car was extracted; no prohibited-contact/stop event was recorded.
